title: Module 4 Challenge: Is This Score Unusual?
scenario: A concentration test is scaled so scores in the population are normally distributed with a mean of 50 and a standard deviation of 10. A clinic says that anyone scoring below 45 "has serious concentration problems" and that a score of 70 "is a once in a lifetime result."

parts.q: What proportion of the population scores below 45?
parts.why: z = −0.50. The proportion below is .3085. Nearly a third of the population scores below 45, so it is hardly a sign of serious problems.

parts.q: What is the z score for a score of 70?
parts.why: z = (70 minus 50)/10 = 2.00. About 2.3 percent of people score higher.

parts.q: Evaluate both of the clinic's claims using proportions. Then say what cutoff you might use if you wanted to flag roughly the lowest 2 percent of scores.
parts.model: About 31 percent of people score below 45 (z = −0.50), so the first claim is unjustified because it labels nearly one in three people as having serious problems. A score of 70 has z = 2.00, and about 2.3 percent of people score at or above it, so it is unusual but not once in a lifetime. About one person in 44 scores that high. To flag the lowest 2 percent I would use a z near −2.05, which gives a raw score of 50 minus 2.05 times 10, about 29.5. A cutoff at about 30 would flag roughly the lowest 2 percent.
check: I used z scores and proportions to judge the claims
I reported the share below 45 and the share above 70
I translated a z cutoff back into a raw score
